- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 7-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (≥0.65) but model forecasts remain flat or declining, adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with sentiment drift.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast window (e.g., 1st–3rd day of 30d) when sentiment is neutral or mildly bearish; apply +0.5–1.0% bias to first 3 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00 → 0.00), model tends to lag; add 1–2 day lag correction to forecast curve.
- If true outcome deviates >1.5% from model in 3–5 consecutive days, apply mean reversion: adjust forecast toward 14-day rolling average of past 14 days.
- For sentiment history with high volatility (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00 → 0.00 → 0.65), model overreacts; dampen forecast volatility by reducing standard deviation of 30d forecast by 20–30%.
